annotation.title_clean: Liability in Robotic Surgery: Legal Frameworks and Case Studies
annotation.title_en: Liability in Robotic Surgery: Legal Frameworks and Case Studies
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Bagwan, M.B.; Joshi, T.; Goswami, R.A.; Patil, R.S.; Sharma, V.; Wani, L.K.
annotation.summary_en: Journal article examining legal liability in robotic surgery, allocating responsibility among surgeons, hospitals and robot manufacturers using case studies. It addresses informed consent, training and maintenance duties, and product defects, and argues that malpractice law and regulation must adapt to evolving surgical technology.
key_provisions_or_claims: Responsibility for robotic surgery errors is split among surgeons, hospitals and manufacturers.
Hospitals may be liable for inadequate training, maintenance and testing of robotic systems.
Manufacturers can be liable for design, hardware or software defects.
Informed consent must cover robot-specific risks such as malfunction and software bugs.
Legal frameworks need updating to keep pace with technology.
